observations:
Torah #240 is a short, self-contained practical teaching of 6 sentences. It does not contain the bechina-style conceptual equating language ('X הוא בְּחִינַת Y', 'X נִקְרָא Y') that is the prerequisite for forming packages. A package requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text forming an independent domain. This Torah contains NONE. 

The teaching operates through a single tight eitza chain: propinquity to the Tzaddik → Mazal receives influence without strain → person receives wealth/children easily. The Mazal is the mediating mechanism, not a conceptual identity. There is no grouping of concepts by shared essential nature here — only a causal mechanism described via mashal (analogy). 

Specifically, the five main concepts of the Torah (צַדִּיק הָאֱמֶת, מַזָּל, הַשְׁפָּעָה, עֲשִׁירוּת/בָּנִים, הִתְקָרְבוּת) are linked by directional flow, not by parallel-nature identity. For example: the Mazal RECEIVES FROM the Tzaddik (eitza), it does not SHARE THE NATURE OF the Tzaddik. Wealth COMES THROUGH the Mazal (eitza), it is not the SAME THING AS the Mazal. 

The sole dataset edge (התקשרות לצדיקים → יוכל לקבל בקל...) is correctly type 'eitza'. No mislabeled edges exist that should be reclassified as bechina. 

Conclusion: Torah #240 is a mashal-based halakhic-advice Torah whose concepts cannot form bechina packages. No new packages should be proposed.
